idiom_name: Codable conformance: nested CodingKeys + custom init(from:)/encode(to:)
implementation_notes: Swift absorbs the translator into protocol conformance: Codable/Decodable+Encodable with a nested CodingKeys enum renames wire keys (case id = "order_id"), and a custom init(from:)/encode(to:) performs value-level conversion through the keyed container (developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/encoding-and-decoding-custom-types). Foundation's JSONDecoder/JSONEncoder provide the format half, including keyDecodingStrategy and dateDecodingStrategy for blanket conventions, so no translator class is written. A separate translator type is justified when one wire format must feed several internal models or when the mapping is versioned per partner.
pitfalls: Synthesised Codable throws on a missing non-optional key but silently ignores unknown keys: a producer-side rename surfaces as a DecodingError with a coding path, while an extra field is dropped without notice - use decodeIfPresent where tolerance is intended.

Key mappings live in the CodingKeys raw values: renaming a Swift property without updating the raw value changes the wire format silently, so pin the raw value for every name that is part of the contract.
dateDecodingStrategy defaults to a deferred (Double since 2001) representation; a payload in ISO-8601 fails at the boundary unless the strategy or an explicit formatter is configured per decoder.
